_comment: HAND-WON FINDINGS. This file exists because they were the one input with no
file to read.
A readiness measure rebuilt from the artifacts enumerates its sources, finds
an artifact for every column except this one, and proceeds without it -- and
reads as MORE rigorous for having done so. That happened: a rebuild on all
four artifacts reported dynamic_dns, port_profile and radius_user ready, and
all three were blocked by facts already measured by hand.
WHAT EACH SOURCE CAN TELL YOU, and the last line is why this file exists:
mapping        field names, dispositions, terraform types
schema         requiredness, element types
model struct   value types
mapper         conditionality, derivation, constants, cross-resource calls
go-unifi SDK   whether a field-masked update exists
prior findings NO FILE -- must be supplied, and this is it
Only the mapper and this file can say whether a surface is READY. The first
three describe what a surface IS; the blockers all live in what it DOES.
Diff any rebuilt measure against this before trusting it. The findings were
measured; an instrument is inferred; the instrument loses.
An EMPTY blocker list means READY TO CUT OVER, not an error. resolved_capabilities
records which blocker kinds have been answered and by what, so a surface whose
last blocker was resolved is visibly ready rather than silently unchanged.
parent-key MEANS CIRCULAR, NOT MERELY ABSENT, and the distinction decides
whether a surface is blocked at all.
resourcekit.Backend closures take (ctx, site, id). An SDK call needing more
is NOT automatically blocked: if the extra argument is derivable from the
object, the closure fetches it. site_to_site_vpn_descriptor.go:276 does
exactly that for DeleteNetwork(ctx, site, id, name) -- it calls GetNetwork
first and reads the name off the result. So network is NOT parent-key
blocked, and neither is anything else with a fetchable extra argument.
WireGuardPeer is different: GetWireGuardPeer(ctx, site, networkID, id)
needs the networkID to perform the lookup that would supply it. A closure
cannot fetch the object to learn the key required to fetch the object. That
circularity is the blocker, and it is why widening Backend is the only
remedy rather than one of several.
It is the only parent-scoped type in go-unifi: of 39 Get methods, 32 take
(site, id), 4 take (site, name) or (site, mac), and 1 takes
(site, networkID, id). One surface, 471 lines -- not enough to widen five
closure signatures across nine working descriptors. Leave it blocked and let
a SECOND parent-scoped surface be the trigger.
sdk-int MEANS THE SDK FIELD IS A PLAIN int, which no field kind can address:
every integer kind in the kit is int64-based (Int64Field, Int64PtrField,
DurationField, DurationPtrField all take func(*S) *int64 or **int64).
power_supervisor is the only MODELLED surface with the problem. Six plain-int
fields, across all three of its types: ConsecutiveFailures on PowerSupervisor,
HeartbeatInterval, SilenceThreshold and PowerOffDuration on
PowerSupervisorSettings, and ClientPsuIndex and PowerSourceIndex on
PowerSupervisorSource. A seventh, HTTPStatusCode in host.go, is an HTTP
envelope rather than a modelled surface. Everything else is int64 or *int64.
COUNTED BY ENUMERATING THE PACKAGE, and the method is recorded because the
first attempt got it wrong in a way the number could not show. That probe
asked go doc about EIGHTEEN TYPE NAMES SOMEBODY TYPED, and returned four --
confidently, with no error, missing PowerSupervisorSource, which is the
nested type the surface's own profile turns on. The correct probe parses all
ninety non-test files of the package and filters for a plain int with a json
tag; it returns seven, which is the six above plus the envelope.
A count whose SCOPE was supplied by its author cannot report what its author
did not think of, and it fails silently rather than loudly. Anyone revisiting
this should re-enumerate rather than trust the six.
SO IT IS LEFT BLOCKED, and NOT on the parent-key cost precedent -- the
remedy is unavailable, which is a stronger reason than expensive.
DO NOT "FIX IT UPSTREAM". go.mod requires github.com/ubiquiti-community/
go-unifi v1.103.0 with NO replace directive, so power_supervisor.go is
UPSTREAM'S FILE. We never modify or open pull requests against that
repository. Routing around it means re-adding a replace onto the fork,
which reopens the dependency decision recorded in the release plan --
public buildability from source -- and that is James's call, not a
blocker-level one.
AND IT IS NOT GENERATOR OUTPUT. power_supervisor.go carries no
"Code generated" marker and no cmd/fields or schemas source mentions
PowerSupervisor -- it is hand-written, so no regeneration would change it
and no capture lock is implicated. An earlier revision of this comment
blamed the generator and pointed the reader at upstream; both were wrong.
NOTE FOR #144: this does NOT block the release. #144 requires COVERAGE for
unifi_power_supervisor, not migration; the surface ships hand-written.
derived-into-blob MEANS THE ATTRIBUTE HAS NO SDK FIELD AND IS RENDERED INTO
ANOTHER ONE. bgp's asn, router_id and peers do not exist on BGPConfig: they
are rendered through a Go template into frr_bgpd_config, and on read they are
copied from the PLAN because nothing can recover them from the config text.
That is two capabilities, not one: a write hook that renders, and a read that
keeps the practitioner's value for an attribute the controller cannot report.
BeforeSend can do the first. The second is close to read-default and is not
the same thing -- a default is a value the provider chooses, this is a value
only the prior plan holds.
undefined-fields MEANS A WRITE CAN SEND A FIELD THE RESOURCE DOES NOT MODEL,
which is measurable. It previously meant an omission whose decision nobody
recorded -- a property NO artifact carries, which is why four instruments
produced four irreconcilable numbers for it. The old sense could not be
checked, so it could not be closed.
THE REMEDY IS ANY UPDATE PATH THAT CANNOT CARRY AN UNMODELLED FIELD, and
four exist. A wire-field mask names what it sends, and the mask is derived
from what the mapper assigns -- TestWireFieldMasksMatchTheirMappers requires
declared == derived, so a field the resource never assigns cannot be named
and is never sent. resourcekit.Backend.UpdateFields masks the same way for
the kit surfaces. Read-modify-write protects client: the unmodelled field
arrives from Get and goes back unchanged. A whole-object write is safe when
every force-emitted field is assigned unconditionally, which is the case for
traffic_route's two.
MEASURED 2026-08-19: zero unprotected across every masked surface. wan's
nine force-emitted fields are exactly mask-intersect-no-omitempty and all
nine are assigned; its other 71 no-omitempty Network fields are off the mask
and never named. network, vpn_client, vpn_server and wlan the same.
THE INSTRUMENT MUST MATCH BOTH ASSIGNMENT FORMS. A first pass over wlan
reported three fields unprotected because it matched only the selector form
'.MinrateNaEnabled' and the mapper writes struct-literal keys
'MinrateNaEnabled:'. That is the same blind spot as the mask check repaired
in #208, reproduced inside the instrument built to check for it. Both forms
or the answer is a plausible false positive.
NOT COVERED BY ANY OF THE FOUR: a force-emitted field assigned under a
null-guard. setting's ips block has four, and they are invisible to every
mask-shaped check precisely BECAUSE they are assigned. See unifi_setting's
migration reason.
RE-DERIVED 2026-08-19 AT d3129c8f. Three blocker kinds were cleared and the
evidence for each is here, because a cleared blocker with no record is the
same defect as a stale one pointing the other way.
no-mapping OFF device, setting, port_forward. #199 decomposed it as "the
resource policy file was never written". All three now have a policy, a
generated package, and a rewired resource -- device and setting on main, and
port_forward's rewire on forgejo awaiting a push nobody has routed around.
device shows two literal schema attributes and they are in its IDENTITY
schema, not its resource schema.
undefined-fields OFF all SEVEN carrying it, not the five that get quoted:
client and traffic_route carry it too. Each has one of the four remedies the
definition above names, and each was read at the call site rather than
inferred. network, vpn_client, vpn_server, wan and wlan have wire-field
masks and measured zero unprotected. client does GetClient, mergeClient,
UpdateClient -- an unmodelled field arrives from the fetch and goes back.
traffic_route builds the whole object from the model, and its two
force-emitted fields, enabled and kill_switch_enabled, are both assigned
unconditionally in a struct literal rather than under a guard.
A REGEX SAID traffic_route WAS READ-MODIFY-WRITE AND IT IS NOT. A loose
multi-line pattern matched a Get and an Update in the same function and
reported a remedy the surface does not use. It reached the right verdict by
the wrong route, which is the failure that survives review. Every one of the
seven was then read directly.
nested OFF the same seven. It is listed in resolved_capabilities in this
file -- ObjectField, ObjectListField and NestedProblems -- so the file
already contained both the claim and its contradiction. Verified rather than
trusted: all three are declared in internal/resourcekit/object_field.go,
firewall_policy uses ObjectField and ObjectListField today, and
NestedProblems is exercised by two test files.
WHAT THAT DOES NOT PROVE, and the caveat is load-bearing. The capability is
complete; whether a given surface's particular nested shape is expressible is
a per-surface fact only its migration can settle. device needed a
set_nested_block, which the general capability had not anticipated, and that
only surfaced at step 4. An empty blocker list here means nothing known
blocks it, not that a migration will be uneventful.
CORRECTION, SAME DAY. I cleared nested off seven surfaces on the strength of
it appearing in resolved_capabilities with a live instance. That was wrong,
and it is reinstated. The capability is real and it does not fit them.
ObjectField is keyed on SDK func(*S) **E and ObjectListField on *[]E: both
need the SDK to HAVE a nested struct for the model's object to correspond to.
Every kit field kind points at exactly one SDK field.
MEASURED ACROSS ALL SEVEN: 24 types.Object fields in their resource models,
and 24 have no backing SDK nested struct. wan alone has ten -- vlan,
egress_qos, dns, dhcp, dhcpv6, smartq, upnp, load_balance, igmp_proxy,
provider_capabilities -- every one a model-side grouping over flat fields of
unifi.Network. vpn_client's wireguard sets network.WireguardPrivateKey,
WireguardClientPresharedKeyEnabled and WireguardInterface, three flat fields
from one object.
POSITIVE CONTROL, and it is what makes the number mean something:
firewall_policy uses ObjectField today and its three objects -- schedule,
source, destination -- are 3 of 3 backed by real nested structs on
ui.FirewallPolicy. The same measure that reports 24 gaps reports zero there.
So the missing capability is a FIELD KIND THAT DISTRIBUTES ONE MODEL OBJECT
ACROSS SEVERAL FLAT SDK FIELDS, which nothing in the kit does. Until it
exists these seven cannot be kit-migrated, and a resolved_capabilities entry
naming nested is true about a mechanism nobody here can use.
THE LESSON IS THE ONE I HAD ALREADY WRITTEN ABOVE AND DID NOT APPLY. "A
complete capability does not promise a given surface's shape is expressible."
I wrote that as a caveat to a clearance I made in the same commit, then
cleared seven surfaces without checking any of their shapes against it. The
caveat was correct and inert -- knowing the failure mode is not the same as
running the check.

resolved_capabilities.SDK-masked-update: Backend.Update plus buildUpdateBody: for an SDK with no Update<T>Fields the kit fetches the current object and applies only the masked fields onto it, so the object sent is the one that came back from Get. client's entry was ALSO stale -- UpdateClientFields exists.
resolved_capabilities.always-wire: AlwaysWire, for wire fields a hook derives that no plan names
resolved_capabilities.list-hooks: Prefetch once + AfterReceive per object in the List path
resolved_capabilities.model-conditional: WriteWhen func(*M) bool, gating ToSDK and SetInPlan
resolved_capabilities.nested: ObjectField for a SingleNested attribute and ObjectListField for a list or block, both with NestedProblems checking the element type for force-emitted members a top-level mask cannot reach
resolved_capabilities.nullable-duration: DurationPtrField, distinguishing nil from a pointer to zero
resolved_capabilities.omit-zero-int: Int64PtrField.OmitZero, a write rule distinct from Elide's read rule
resolved_capabilities.pointer-string: StringLikePtrField, omitting the empty string the controller rejects
resolved_capabilities.preWriteHook: Prefetch/BeforeSend/AfterReceive, now wired into Read and Update as well as Create
resolved_capabilities.read-default: ReadDefault on StringField, substituted in ToModel so the list path gets it too
resolved_capabilities.typed-collection: StringSetField.ElementType for the state element type, plus KeepPrior for the spelling already in state -- a Set identifies members by string value, so the element type's semantic equality never reaches the set
